changes: Autocomplete and the command palette add backticks to database, table, and column names that need them.
Opening a failed view's INSERT from the table details asks before running it, as the INSERT viewer does.
Autocomplete no longer freezes on a very long line.
A server that sends a malformed column type, or thousands of columns with one name, can no longer stall a query or end it without an error.
The menu bar has File and Query menus: New Tab, Reopen Closed Tab, Close Tab, Save, Run, Run All, Cancel, and Format, each with its shortcut.
⌘⇧L formats your query from anywhere in the window. Before, it worked only inside the editor.
In the results grid, hovering a cell shows its full text only when the text is cut off.
The row count, the time, Copy, and Export sit above the results grid, beside the Results, Chart, and Profile tabs.
Settings has a Theme choice: Light, Dark, or Auto. The theme button in the sidebar is gone.
In the Schema sidebar, double-click a table to preview its first 100 rows.
In the column panel, Cancel stops a running stats scan, and a clock shows how long it has run.
Closing the column panel, or picking another column, stops the scan on the server.
Right-click a cell in the results grid for Copy, Copy as Markdown, Inspect cell, Find, and Select all.
In the results grid, Shift+click extends the selection to the cell you click.
You can sort a column from the keyboard: Tab to its sort button, then press Enter.
The Help menu has Keyboard Shortcuts, and the app menu has Settings… (⌘,).
⌘T opens a new tab, as ⌘N does.
The left and right arrow keys move between editor tabs.
In the Schema sidebar, the arrow keys move through databases, tables, and columns.
In the Schema sidebar, materialized views have their own icon.
When the Schema sidebar, the table panel, the dependency graph, or Saved fails to load, it shows the server's message and a Retry button.
When a connection fails to load, the sidebar says so instead of asking you to pick a connection.
Query History says "No queries match" when a search finds nothing.
In Settings, each switch sits above the option it turns on.
⌘A outside a text field no longer highlights the whole window.
When a query runs past the server's time limit, the error tells you how to allow more time.
Undo and redo stay within each tab.
After you switch tabs, Run picks the statement under the cursor in that tab.
Results show dates before 1970. Before, those queries failed.
If the app hits an unexpected error, it shows the message and a Reload button instead of a blank window.
Query History and the table panel's Parts & merges section show the error and a Retry button when they fail to load.
In Monitor → Live Queries, the "yours" tag marks every query your user runs.
The connection form warns you when Secure (TLS) is off for a remote server.
Table and database names that contain a backslash no longer break the app's own queries.
When a server sends malformed data, the app shows an error instead of quitting or freezing.
A JSON column inside another type, such as Array(JSON), returns an error that tells you to wrap it in toJSONString().
Panels no longer wait silently when macOS reports no internet connection.
The app's messages and labels use plainer English.
The app uses an updated TLS library with security fixes.
Small windows leave more room for results.
In the ⌘P palette, the tables section reads "Insert table name": picking a table types its name into your query.
The Schema sidebar hides the storage tables of materialized views.
In the Schema sidebar, hover a table to see its type.
Times read "5m ago". Hover a time to see the exact time in your time zone.
The Logs panel shows times in your time zone.
You can use the editor while the table or column panel is open.
Error messages stay on screen until you close them.
The Logs panel tells read-only users that the server sends them no logs. Before, it kept waiting for logs.
The connection form opens with the cursor in the Name field.
Press Enter in the connection form to save the connection.
The connection form marks each missing field in red.
In the connection form, turning off Secure (TLS) switches the port from 9440 to 9000.
In the connection form, pasting a URL into Host keeps only the host name.
In Monitor → Live Queries, a Stop button replaces the ✕.
In Monitor → Live Queries, the Stop button appears only on queries you are allowed to stop.
In Monitor → Live Queries, a message confirms each stopped query.
Opening a saved query that is already open switches to its tab.
Tabs opened from History take their name from the query.
A new tab never takes the name of a tab that is already open.
If macOS refuses to share a connection's password, the sidebar says so under the connection picker and offers Retry and Edit.
The connection form stays open when you press Esc or click outside it.
A double-click on Run runs the query once.
While a query runs, a line under the toolbar shows how long it has run and how far it got.
Run all labels its result: "Result of statement 3 of 3".
The last result stays on screen, dimmed, until the new one arrives.
Charting a table by a category counts the rows in each category.
A new look, closer to a native Mac app.
Wide results scroll sideways, so you can reach the last column.
Closing a tab with a running query asks you to confirm.
Closing any other tab offers Undo.
After an update installs, choose Restart now or Later.
Before restarting for an update, the app warns you if a query is still running.
In Monitor → Activity, "View INSERT" shows a failed view's INSERT, read-only.
Running that INSERT again from a tab asks you to confirm.
In the Schema sidebar, "Preview 100 rows" shows the rows right away. For Kafka and other queue tables, it still opens the query without running it.
In the Schema sidebar, the ⋯ menu next to each table inserts the table's name into your query or copies it.
In the Schema sidebar, right-click a table to open its ⋯ menu.
The Activity count matches the rows marked "new".
The Activity count leaves out queries that failed on a typo.
Each materialized view failure has a "Copy for LLM" button.
A new app icon.
The app quotes text parameters: {country} with the value US sends 'US'. To insert a column name or other raw SQL, write {!name}.
Braces in comments and regexes no longer create parameters.
The Monitor panels reconnect after a dropped connection. They stop only on errors that a retry cannot fix.
⌘P, ⌘S, ⌘W and the other shortcuts work again.
Each server error has a "Copy for LLM" button. It copies the error, its last message, and a query to look it up.
The results grid tells you when it stops at 10,000 rows.
"Run without limit" fetches the rows past 10,000.
Copied cells paste into spreadsheets as separate cells.
Search finds tables as well as databases.
The table drawer lists columns first.
Column stats load only when you click.
Column stats work for read-only users.
The toolbar names the connection your query runs on.
Deleting a connection tells you how many saved queries it also deletes.
One Monitor tab holds Server Activity, Kafka, and Live Queries.
Each Monitor panel shows when it last updated and has a Refresh button.
A failed query has a "Copy for LLM" button. It copies the SQL as run, the full error, and the server version, ready to paste into any LLM.
A long error scrolls in its own pane.
The toolbar no longer repeats the error.
ClickHouse's system.query_log names ch-gui as the client, with your user and machine, as it does for clickhouse-client.
In system.query_log, ch-gui's background checks have a client name ending in "(monitor)", so you can filter them out.
Decimals below one display correctly: 0.05 no longer shows as 5.
Whole numbers display without a stray trailing dot.
256-bit numbers display instead of failing.
The results grid numbers its rows. Click a row number to select the row, or click # to select all rows.
Copied rows leave out the row numbers.
Dates, text, and enums inside arrays, tuples, and maps display as plain values.
Columns that share a name all appear: SELECT 1, 1 shows two columns.
Column names and errors with unusual characters no longer break the query.
Columns with named tuples, such as Array(Tuple(name String, value String)), display instead of failing the whole query.
Enum columns show their labels (for example TIMEOUT_EXCEEDED) instead of numeric codes.
On ClickHouse 26.3, the Kafka consumer details work again.
On ClickHouse 26.3, the table drawer's projections section works again.
Server Activity, Live Queries, and Kafka refresh only while their tab is open.
Two editor tabs on the same connection each keep their own progress bar and server logs.
Editing a connection's host, user, password, or certificate takes effect on the next query instead of after a restart.
Switching between sidebar tabs no longer refreshes a panel that has just refreshed.
Leaving the Errors, Live Queries, or Kafka tab open no longer opens thousands of connections an hour to your ClickHouse cluster.
If your account can't run cluster-wide queries, the monitoring tabs read only the node you are connected to, instead of showing repeated permission errors.
The app remembers that choice for each connection.
Live Queries and Server Activity refresh less often by default. Change how often in Settings.
Querying a table with AggregateFunction columns shows an error instead of an empty result. The error names the column and suggests finalizeAggregation() or a -Merge combinator.
SimpleAggregateFunction columns display their values like any other column.
An error while loading a result shows as an error instead of an empty "No rows returned." grid.
After such an error, the next query reconnects on its own.
In the results grid, double-click a cell or press Enter on it to see the whole value in a popup.
The value popup formats JSON values and has a Raw toggle.
Copy in the value popup copies exactly what is on screen and keeps every digit of 19-digit IDs.
A new Copy ▾ menu on the results toolbar copies the whole result as CSV, TSV, a Markdown table, JSON rows, SQL VALUES tuples, or a Python list.
The Export button offers CSV, TSV, or JSON Lines.
A SELECT with no LIMIT returns at most 10,000 rows, so an accidental SELECT * on a billion-row table can't freeze the app or overload the server.
An amber "auto-LIMIT hit" badge shows when the 10,000-row limit left more rows behind.
A switch on each tab turns off the 10,000-row limit.

A new Δ button in the sidebar lists every server setting that your profile or admin changed from ClickHouse's defaults. Check it first when a query behaves differently on this connection than elsewhere.
A new Samples section in the Saved sidebar holds 10 ready-to-run health checks, such as top tables by disk, slowest queries, and replica lag.
The table drawer has a Copy DDL button.
The table drawer's Copy names button copies the column names, comma-separated, ready for a SELECT list.
Cancelling a query shows "Query cancelled" instead of a red error.
Cancelling a multi-statement script stops the whole script, not only the current statement.
While a query runs, the toolbar shows which connection it runs on.
While a script runs, the toolbar shows the current statement, for example "Statement 2 of 5".
Closing a tab during a query stops the query on the server.
After you switch connections, the schema, function docs, and activity panels show only the new server's data.
Cancel always stops the query on the server where it started.
Re-running the same query keeps your column widths and sort order.
Copying from the grid shows a "Copied" message.
In History, back-to-back runs of the same statement share one row.
History deletes unpinned entries after 90 days and never overwrites pinned entries.
Keyboard shortcuts no longer act behind an open dialog. Before, ⌘W could close a tab you could not see.
⌘. cancels a running query even with a drawer open.
Editing a connection keeps its saved password.
Drag across the results grid to select a range of cells.
Copy a selected range with ⌘C, which pastes into spreadsheets, or with ⌘⇧C as a Markdown table.
Extend a selected range with ⇧ and the arrow keys.
Your open tabs keep their SQL, titles, and parameter values after you quit the app.
Deleting a connection works again. Before, the confirmation dialog never appeared, so Delete did nothing.
The progress bar and server logs no longer freeze partway through fast queries.
Pressing ⌘↵ while a query is running no longer mixes up two runs in the same tab.
Sorting a column clears the row selection. Before, ⌘C could copy a different row than the one you picked.
All tabs run on the connection selected in the sidebar dropdown. Before, queries kept running on the connection the app started with.
Press ⌘⇧C to copy results as a Markdown table: the whole grid, or the selected cell, row, or column.
After the app updates, What's New lists the changes.
Open What's New any time from Help → What's New.
The "update available" dialog shows the release notes for the version you are about to install.
⌘↵ runs the statement under the cursor, or the selected text.
As you move the cursor, the editor highlights the statement that ⌘↵ will run.
⌘⇧↵ or the new "Run all" button runs everything in the editor. ⌘A then ⌘↵ also works.
Empty results read "No rows returned." instead of showing a blank grid.
